structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single CANDIDATE architecture/design document for the Pre-Python gate at docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/persistence-and-evidence.md, limited to persistence and evidence design, with only local packet/readiness evidence allowed to change. The work is documentation-only and must preserve existing Founder/EOS/Node evidence, label proposed architecture as candidate, avoid implementation, and record unresolved Founder decisions instead of silently deciding them.
structuredContent.summary: The requested work has a clear bounded outcome: draft one reviewable candidate design artifact covering operational-state persistence and Engineering Trajectory / Quality Evidence persistence, using specified authority and historical evidence. The scope is cohesive because both rows concern the persistence model’s separation of operational state, durable evidence, learned policy, retention, redaction, identity, transaction, crash recovery, and migration semantics. The task explicitly forbids source/config/test/runtime changes and implementation approval, which keeps expected rework local to the document.
implementation_unknowns: Exact contents and wording of the cited local source baselines and existing architecture documents must be inspected during drafting; the assessment cannot independently verify them from the supplied text.
The existing documentation style, packet/readiness evidence conventions, and checker expectations need to be followed when creating the artifact.

The drafter must determine how to map Node JSON snapshots, dispatcher behavior, delivery IDs, state compatibility, and lifecycle evidence into design constraints without treating Node implementation accidents as canonical architecture.
The drafter must identify which persistence semantics are already Founder-resolved versus which should be presented as candidate options/tradeoffs for later Founder approval.
The drafter must formulate successful and failing examples that are traceable to the cited authority and do not invent unstated implementation details.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable by reviewing the produced document and local packet/readiness evidence against the named G21/G22 rows, binding Founder authority, EOS requirements, and cited Node evidence. A single independent content-review verdict is meaningful because the artifact is one candidate design document with traceable source/invariant mapping, explicit contract semantics, examples, scope limitations, and recorded unresolved Founder decisions. Runtime regression execution is explicitly out of scope and not required for this documentation-only packet.
material_risks: The document could accidentally promote candidate persistence/storage semantics to approved architecture instead of labeling them for Founder review.
The drafter could overfit to Node implementation details or historical logs rather than extracting deliberate architecture constraints.
The operational-state, trajectory evidence, Quality Evidence, and learned-policy boundaries could be blurred, undermining a central acceptance requirement.
Retention, redaction, lineage, immutable accepted evidence, crash recovery, and migration semantics may expose material Founder decisions that must be recorded rather than resolved by the agent.
Cross-document dependencies could be adopted implicitly instead of cited as candidate or unresolved, contrary to the instructions.
Including private chain-of-thought, secrets, private logs, or implementation changes would violate the explicit exclusions.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the bounded candidate design document and its local packet/readiness evidence only, using the cited baselines and authority, with any material unresolved Founder choices recorded as explicit questions/options in the artifact.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the supplied packet establishes a specific documentation-only outcome, bounded paths, governing authority, exclusions, acceptance criteria, and verification method. No material owner-intent question prevents drafting: the task explicitly says to stop only at a genuine owner decision preventing candidate drafting, otherwise produce a reviewable candidate with options and tradeoffs. The operational and evidence persistence topics are semantically coupled under the pre-Python persistence model rather than independent decision centers requiring separate execution. Remaining uncertainties are implementation/document-research tasks for the drafter, not readiness blockers.
